name: Window length (hours)
description: How much BSV history the client keeps. Sets the deposit deadline

name: Window length (records)
description: window_hours × 3600 / seconds_per_block. Bounded above by the account cap

name: Target block spacing
description: BSV's ten-minute target

name: Bytes per header record
description: 32 hash + 16 chainwork + 4 time. Not configurable

name: DAA lookback (records)
description: 144 + 3 for the median-of-three. Measured: 146 reproduces 0/324 headers, 147 reproduces 324/324

name: Difficulty rule
description: The rule BSV actually uses. Verified against real mainnet headers. Hard-coded (X3)

name: Lower clamp
description: Multiplies seconds_per_block, not the averaging window

name: Upper clamp
description: As above

name: Confirmation depth
description: MIN_CONFIRMATIONS, fixed in code, not a runtime parameter

name: Headers per fork tx
description: Set by the 1,232-byte transaction limit

name: Solana account cap
description: A Solana limit, not a choice

name: Deployment identifier
description: Binds a deposit to one deployment (P11). Must differ per cluster. Not built — the code checks only that the recipient's 32 bytes appear in the OP_RETURN

name: Maximum target
description: Regtest uses 0x207fffff; mainnet 0x1d00ffff. In code as MAINNET_POW_LIMIT_BITS, with no_retargeting derived from the regtest value

name: Freshness bound
description: How recent the last accepted header must be before release. A multiple of BSV block time — ~1,500 Solana slots per block. Implemented (StaleClient), untested on a local validator

name: Maturity
description: How deep a deposit's block must be before its staged mint releases, in BSV blocks. 144 blocks is about 24 hours at BSV's 600 s target. This is the window in which a reorg is caught and the mint burned. Constraint: confirmations + maturity <= window, so 12 + 144 <= 192. SET TO 144: at 0 the mint side had no window at all, and an affordable rented reorg could not be reversed.

name: Detection margin
value: 48 blocks at the designed values der
description: window − maturity. Do not add floor into this subtraction. Zero at the maximum committed depth

name: Rent refund on close
description: Closing an item returns its rent to the caller

name: Mint-side bond — BSV side (the float)
description: Held outside the reserve. The bond is the float — working capital for transfers — not a capital requirement sized against the reserve, and not a capacity ceiling. The k × (BSV held) line is a solvency check on mint and exit. Held under the collective (threshold ECDSA) key, not the member's own, and seized by the members collectively; slashing pays the slashers from it. A collective action by the majority, not an automatic rule

name: Mint-side bond custody
description: The design requirement the mechanism rests on. If a member controls their own bond they move it the moment they are caught. Residuals: a majority could seize an honest member's bond; nothing on BSV compels signing, so the duty to slash is social

name: Redeem-side bond — solBSV side (the float)
description: Seizable on Solana. This side is enforceable. Neither bond sits inside the reserve

name: Nominal bond size
description: Superseded by the two side-specific bonds; kept as the per-side default name

name: Aggregate bond (tracked)
description: The old single running total is replaced by two side-specific aggregates

name: Bonds gate minting
description: F5. A mint is refused unless the BSV-side bond covers the BSV held after it. A solvency floor, not a capacity claim. The old total_bond ≥ k × (non_bonded_supply + amount) is superseded

name: Bond denomination
description: Mint side BSV, redeem side solBSV; neither inside the reserve. No price oracle is needed for either

name: Against a colluding threshold
description: Stated risk, not a mechanism. No on-chain predicate proves who signed an off-chain threshold signature. The maximum loss is the whole non-member supply. Publishing the reserve and supply converts a hidden theft into a visible one; the unchallenged-spend case is separately addressed by the reported spent-outpoint record

name: Bond coverage floor
description: bsv_bond ≥ k × (BSV held) and solbsv_bond ≥ k × (solBSV held), checked on mint and exit. A solvency check, not a capacity ceiling. The capacity arithmetic built on k and n/t is withdrawn. Capital inefficiency accepted

name: Gateway signing threshold
description: t of n for the gateway threshold ECDSA key. N is a variable; the number is arbitrary and deferred. The key emits one signature and is one leg of the reserve's 2-of-2 script. Changing t or n is a re-sharing, not a migration

name: Gateway roster size (N)
description: The N of 4-of-N: how many members hold a share of the gateway threshold key. The shape is settled and the number is deferred, so the registry stores a floor and never an N. The program reads the live roster from the member records and refuses any departure that would take the bonded set below fed.threshold.

name: Re-sharing ceremony
description: How a newly admitted member is given a share of the live gateway key: generation, distribution and verification. Not specified anywhere. admit_member records the admission and does not perform the ceremony, so the registry names a member the key does not yet know.

name: Leaver-share invalidation
description: Nothing invalidates a departing member's share. leave_member returns the bonds and records MemberStatus::Left, and the share stays valid off chain, so the effective threshold degrades with churn: at 4-of-N four former members together still hold four valid shares. A known unfinalised problem, not a mechanism.

name: Removal and compelled exit
description: Whether a member can be removed without leaving, who may do it, and whether a member can be compelled to stay. Not specified. No instruction removes a member: the registry has admission, record_bonds, leave_member and a solBSV-side seizure, and none of the four removes a seat without the member's own signature.

name: Greycore size
description: The second signer set on the reserve script: trusted third parties, not node operators — people with reputations to lose, who do not run the reserve. The Greycore finds and admits replacement members

name: Greycore threshold
description: How many Greycore keys must sign alongside the gateway. The Greycore co-signs every reserve spend, which is what constrains the reserve. 4-of-5 was an earlier proposal and is not settled

name: Shard count
description: One key or several groups. Affects blast radius and latency. There is no sharding today: blast radius is 100%

name: Unbonding period
description: Must exceed the redemption deadline plus the challenge window

name: Delegated staking
description: Phase 2. Lets non-members delegate solBSV to a member and share its fee. Activatable by governance, not built

name: Reserve deposit script
value: 2-of-2 OP_CHECKMULTISIG dec, shape accepted in code built
description: OP_2 <gateway threshold key> <greycore key> OP_2 OP_CHECKMULTISIG. Both keys must sign; the Greycore polices every reserve spend. The committed code accepts this shape: is_reserve_multisig, MAX_SCRIPT_LEN = 71, DepositScript::SPACE = 84. The keys/quorum behind it are not built

name: BSV-side bond seizure
description: The Solana program cannot seize the BSV-side bond; the members sign a threshold transaction. Stated as a residual, not hidden

name: Spent-outpoint record (N5)
value: one PDA per (txid, vout), written by the program authority built
description: report_spent records a deposit outpoint the reserve has spent; verify_deposit refuses a deposit whose outpoint is in the record. The signer is the upgrade authority — a PoC stand-in for the federation, which does not exist yet. Permanent and rent-exempt with no prune: closing a record would re-open the mint of an already-spent deposit

name: Pass threshold
description: Share of pledged coins required

name: Delay before effect
description: Reducible by governance, but never below gov.delay_min. Redemptions run throughout

name: Minimum delay (floor)
description: F7. Both readings are defensible and the choice is open: with a floor, a majority cannot take the warning away — proposal 1 can only shorten the delay to the floor, so proposal 2 still has to be exited during it; without, the exit window is whatever the current majority allows. A judgement about trust, not a correctness question

name: Signal from proposal
description: Live from the moment it is raised

name: Governance owns the upgrade key
description: Deliberate. Nothing is immutable, so the exit window, not the rule, is the protection

name: Checkpoint/pause authority
value: federation threshold designed — in code it is the upgrade authority, one key, timelocked
description: F4. Replaces the single deployer key. No timelock-free path to rewriting the checkpoint. Not built

name: Authority timelock
description: TIMELOCK_SLOTS, a PoC value. Applied to propose_authority_change / execute_authority_change / cancel_authority_change. Must be long enough to exit

name: Pause threshold
description: Lower than a governance change, because the power is bounded

name: Pause auto-lift
description: Days before a pause lapses unless renewed

name: Peg-in fee (gross)
description: Covers all transaction fees; the remainder is member income. Its physical location is unspecified — N1

name: Peg-out fee (gross)
description: As above

name: Challenger bounty
description: Share of a slashed bond paid to whoever proves the misbehaviour. The burn_staged bounty is suggested, not sized, and not built

name: Minimum deposit
description: The floor verify_deposit enforces on a deposit output, in the base units the claim's amount is in (1 BSV at 8 decimals). MIN_PEG_IN = 100,000,000 in code. Prices out dust griefing

name: Legacy replay-list cap
description: Replaced by a nullifier PDA per deposit, which is built. There is no list and no ceiling

name: Deposit commitment
value: version ‖ cluster_id ‖ program_hash ‖ flags ‖ recipient dec
description: Designed. What is built checks only that the recipient's 32 bytes appear in an OP_RETURN

name: Payout depth
description: BSV confirmations before a payout is provable. C_payout

name: Challenge window
description: W. Confirmations a payout needs before settling

name: Redemption deadline
description: How long a member has to pay before the holder may cancel. In Solana SLOTS, because a height deadline would never expire if the header feed stalled. NOTE: the earlier claim that this must exceed payout_confirmations + challenge_window does NOT hold at these values (216,000 slots against 150 BSV blocks). The pay-and-refund race is closed structurally instead -- cancel_redeem is refused while a claim is live.

name: Cancellation grace
description: Cancellation is immediate on expiry. A grace period would only delay the exit

name: Minimum redemption
description: Minimum redemption, so a claim's proof is worth the transaction fees to settle

name: Concurrent redemption cap
description: Cap on concurrent pending redemptions, so the escrow cannot be used to make the program's per-instruction work unbounded

name: Solana rent
description: (bytes + 128) × 5,080. The 128-byte overhead is inside this rate. 6,960 is an older toolchain's constant and overstates by ~37%. Measured: solana rent 0 = 650,240 lamports; solana rent 165 = 1,488,440

name: Solana base fee
description: Per signature

name: Transaction size
description: Solana limit; drives lc.max_fork_batch
